title: Automating the SOC: Building an Autonomous Threat-Hunting Agent
summary: Security Operations Center analysts are drowning in false-positive alerts. Learn how to build a Blue Team Agent that autonomously investigates SIEM alerts and instantly quarantines compromised endpoints.

body.text: Automating the SOC: Building an Autonomous Threat-Hunting Agent

elements.text: Security Operations Center (SOC) analysts are drowning in thousands of false-positive alerts daily. By the time a human investigates a legitimate alert, ransomware has already encrypted critical file shares. In this guide, we will build a

elements.definition: An autonomous defensive AI that triages security alerts, investigates indicators of compromise, and executes remediation.

elements.text: that autonomously investigates SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) alerts, traces lateral network movement, and instantly quarantines compromised endpoints before malware can spread.
Prerequisites: Basic understanding of SIEM platforms (like Splunk or Elastic Security), network topologies, and Python.

Think of the agent as a digital immune system. The SIEM triggers an alert (the 'symptom'). The agent autonomously pulls the raw logs, correlates the endpoint's recent outbound network connections, and uses an LLM to determine if the activity matches a known adversary profile. If confirmed, the agent applies the 'cure' by dynamically updating the network switch or firewall to isolate the infected machine.

elements.text: The core of the agent is the triage and remediation loop. The code below demonstrates how the agent intercepts an alert and executes an API call to a firewall manager.

body.code:
def handle_siem_alert(alert_id, endpoint_ip):
    logs = siem.get_recent_logs(endpoint_ip)
    
    # Ask LLM to evaluate the logs for lateral movement patterns
    evaluation = llm.evaluate_threat_level(logs)
    
    if evaluation.confidence > 0.90 and evaluation.is_malicious:
        print(f'[CRITICAL] Lateral movement detected on {endpoint_ip}')
        # Execute Network Quarantine
        firewall.isolate_host(endpoint_ip)
        slack.send_alert(f'Host {endpoint_ip} autonomously isolated. Reason: {evaluation.reason}')
    else:
        print('[INFO] Alert resolved as false positive.')

elements.text: This script bypasses the human analyst queue. If the LLM identifies the logs as malicious with high confidence, it directly triggers the `firewall.isolate_host()` command, effectively shutting down the attack path in milliseconds.

The danger of autonomous remediation is blocking legitimate business operations. If a developer runs a massive data migration script that mimics data exfiltration, the agent might quarantine a critical database server. Always implement an
of critical infrastructure IPs that the agent is strictly forbidden from isolating.

To validate the agent, deploy a synthetic malware detonator (like Atomic Red Team) on an isolated staging VM. Ensure the agent correctly identifies the PowerShell obfuscation techniques, outputs the threat JSON, and cuts network access to the VM.
We built an autonomous Blue Team agent capable of slashing Mean Time To Respond (MTTR) from 30 minutes down to less than a second, neutralizing ransomware before it encrypts the network.

items: Implement a fast-path un-quarantine mechanism via Slack buttons for analysts to quickly reverse false positives.
Integrate the agent with endpoint detection agents (like CrowdStrike) for process-level termination capabilities.
Expand the LLM's context by feeding it the MITRE ATT&CK framework vectors.
